# Unbiased Mold Inspections

> Independent mold inspection for Indiana. Mycotoxin correlation specialist who
> uses mycotoxin test results to locate hidden growth substrates. Sells no
> remediation services, and takes no payment from remediation companies for
> referrals, so there is no conflict of interest.

Certified Professional Inspector: Josh Underwood. Based in Indianapolis, Indiana.
Phone: (317) 210-0319. Covers the state of Indiana and surrounding areas, and can
travel to neighboring states if needed.

## What makes this inspector different

- No remediation services are sold, so there is no incentive to find a problem.
- No remediation company pays to appear on a "recommended list."
- Specialises in helping naturopathic and holistic medicine providers locate
  hidden sources of mycotoxin exposure.
- Remediation consultations are included at no extra charge.
- Initial advice is free.

## Services

- Whole home inspection for mold and moisture intrusion issues
- Remediation consultations, no extra charge
- Genus identification
- Nationally accredited laboratory results
- A variety of sample collection options, customised per inspection
- Clearance testing for real-estate transactions

## Method

Mycotoxin correlation. Blood and urine mycotoxin panels show what the body is
able to purge, which can understate exposure when the body cannot clear a
particular toxin. Growth substrates and growth conditions are used to infer which
toxins are likely accumulating. Where no doctor's lab results exist, spore trap
analysis is used with inductive and deductive reasoning instead.

Mycotoxins investigated: ochratoxin, aflatoxin, gliotoxin, trichothecenes.

## Turnaround

Sample results take about four business days. Mold samples do not need to
culture.

DEPLOYMENT NOTE (remove this section before publishing)

llms.txt is only read at the root of a domain — https://example.com/llms.txt.
Sitting in this demo subdirectory it has no effect. When this redesign goes live
on unbiasedmoldinspections.in, move this file to the domain root.

Also worth knowing: llms.txt is a proposed convention, not a ratified standard,
and no major AI provider has publicly confirmed that it reads one. It costs
nothing and is easy to keep accurate, but the things that demonstrably drive AI
citation are being crawlable, stating facts plainly, and being referenced from
other sites. Those are already handled on the page itself.
